conviction_note: Modest positive lean: the Q3 guide (16% growth at the midpoint) looks conservative against Q2's 22% fleet growth, a ~$20M sequential SBC step-down and two European peers (Voi revenue +53%, Dott rides/vehicle +22%) that printed strong Q3s after Lime last spoke, set against Citizens' public-trip-data read that US trips slowed (already reflected in a ~26% fall since mid-September); p_up 55 on an abs move of 13 gives +1.3, close to the +0.9 sum of the findings, and both are small because every positive is a proxy or lands inside the guide and the stock already popped +10% into the print.

EBITDA $265-285M, capex $180-185M (Q2 8-K ex-99.1, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1699963/000114036126031146/ef20079411_ex99-1.htm, 2026-08-04). positioning_check: No options market (baseline: no_options_market), so no skew and no implied move. Short interest ~1.3M shares, ~2.6% of float, days to cover 2.9, as of early September 2026 (Stock Titan via search snippet, https://www.stocktitan.net/overview/LIME/); FINRA 2026-07-31 settlement 1.1M shares, DTC 4.8 (curvedtrading snippet, https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/lime/short-interest/, page 403); a borrow fee of 22.4% shown in a curvedtrading snippet (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/lime/), unverified. Not a crowded short. Float is small: IPO sold only 6.96M shares of 64.0M outstanding (424B4), with a 160-day lock-up ending about 2026-12-07. Stock closed $22.58 on 2026-11-02, near the 52w low $22.07 and the $25 IPO price, -49% from the $44.38 high, below its 50-day MA of $30.65; it traded +10% to ~$24.9 intraday on 2026-11-03 on light volume (64,680 shares by midday against a 361k average, MarketBeat). Analysts: 9 Buy / 2 Hold, avg target ~$37.

findings.finding: Citizens (Andrew Boone) cut its LIME target to $33 from $45 on 2026-10-26, saying its tracking of public trip data shows US trip growth slowed in Q3, the World Cup benefit faded, weather was likely a headwind and Lime seems to have traded trip growth for pricing in Q2 and is moving away from LimePrime to drive frequency. Citizens still expects Q3 revenue 'near the high end' of the $340-360M guide, so the negative is about volume quality and the forward guide rather than the reported quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Only one public print (Q2, 2026-08-04): revenue +24% with fleet +22% and the first guide; bought +14.5% close-to-close (baseline) after an +8.8% pre-print day. Not a trustworthy base rate. Trip and volume metrics have never been reported to the public, so this line has no reaction history.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. It is a public note, and the stock fell from $30.49 on 2026-09-15 (CEO Form 4 withholding price) to $22.58 on 2026-11-02. What is not priced is whether management's Q4 guide confirms the US slowdown; had the market fully discounted a guide cut, the stock would not sit with a ~$37 average target and 9 Buys. Sized small.
findings.independence: Partly offset, not confirmed: Seattle data (GeekWire) shows strong US city ridership but is World Cup-weighted, which is consistent with Citizens' 'World Cup faded'. No second source confirms the US slowdown.

findings.finding: Two European micromobility peers printed strong Q3s after Lime last guided (2026-08-04). Voi (2026-10-22): Q3 net revenue EUR 88.2M, +53% y/y from EUR 57.5M, net revenue per vehicle per day +10% to EUR 5.36 on 40% more active vehicles, EBIT EUR 16.9M vs 8.1M, and 'stable regulation' in Paris letting it expand its fleet. Dott (2026-10-23): Q3 net revenue EUR 55.6M, back to top-line growth on rides per vehicle +22% y/y (but FY adj. EBITDA guided to the lower end, EUR 30-32M). Europe is a large part of Lime's base, and Lime's guide implies revenue per vehicle falling (16% revenue growth against a fleet that grew 22% in Q2), so peers showing per-vehicle usage rising in Q3 point to upside on that implied deceleration.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: One print only: Q2's revenue +24% with the first guide bought +14.5%. No history of Lime reacting to peer prints.
findings.why_not_priced: Voi and Dott are private bond and VC-backed issuers that report on Swedish and company sites, and none of LIME's US sell-side headlines since mid-October cites them. The only visible Q3 read (Citizens) is US-only and negative. Had the market taken a strong European Q3 into account, the stock would not be trading at the 52-week low with consensus revenue only $2M above the guide midpoint.
findings.independence: Dott Q3 release (different company, different document): https://www.webull.com/news/15796028128011264 (2026-10-23). It is a proxy: neither peer names Lime, Voi is gaining share, and Dott's lower-end EBITDA guide cuts against margin read-through. Lime's regional split is not disclosed in the Q2 release, so the European weight is not quantified.

findings.finding: Lime's own Q2 call and release show a guide built conservatively, but the upside lands inside the guided range. Q3 revenue $340-360M is 16% growth at the midpoint, against Q2 revenue +24% and fleet +22% with fleet 'tracking ahead of schedule'. The CFO said a Q2 SBC step-up won't repeat (~$20M sequential benefit), gross margin typically rises 300-400bp from Q2 to Q3, and 'we anticipate achieving operating leverage in Q3'. The street sits at $352.3M (above the $350M midpoint), so a print at the $360M top end is a ~2% revenue beat.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 was the first print and beat a near-zero EPS consensus on one-offs (tax valuation allowance); stock +14.5% on revenue growth, debt paydown and the guide. One observation only.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: consensus is already in the upper half of the guide at $352.3M. What is not priced is the fleet-versus-revenue gap: a guide that implies revenue per vehicle down ~5 points after Q2's +1.5 leaves room above $360M that the $346-358M estimate range does not cover. Kept small because it lands inside what the company guided.
findings.independence: Shares the fleet-growth fact with the peer finding (the Q2 8-K, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1699963/000114036126031146/ef20079411_ex99-1.htm), but the evidence differs: this one is Lime's own guide construction, the other is peer per-vehicle demand. Citizens' 'near the high end' points the same way on revenue.

findings.finding: GeekWire reports that Lime topped 10.5M Seattle rides in 2026 by October, passing its full-year 2025 total (10.5M per SDOT, itself +60% on 2024) two months early. Four of the top five ridership days were World Cup days, including 83,000+ trips on 2026-06-19.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None; city ride data has never been tested against a LIME print.
findings.source_date: 2026-10 (URL path /2026/; article says 'into October'; page body returned 403, details from search snippets)
findings.why_not_priced: It is local press. But it is one city, weighted to June and July, and it does not contradict Citizens' broader public-trip read that US Q3 trips slowed after the World Cup. Sized at almost nothing because a narrow proxy loses to a broader series.
findings.independence: SDOT blog for the 2025 base (https://sdotblog.seattle.gov/tag/lime/). It argues partly against the Citizens finding, but at a smaller scale.

findings.finding: LIME rose ~10% intraday on 2026-11-03 before the print, to ~$24.9 from a $22.58 close, on light volume (64,680 shares by midday against a 361k average) and with no stated cause. The baseline seals spot at $24.945, so part of any relief rally from the 52-week low happened before the entry.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 had the same shape: +8.8% on the print day before the release, then +14.5% the next session. One prior, and it went the other way.
findings.why_not_priced: It is the price itself. Filed because it sets the entry: a +10% move on 18% of average volume is positioning, not information, and it reduces the gap a beat has to close. Sized near 0 because an unexplained move carries no evidence of its own.

outside_window.finding: IPO lock-up: under the 424B4, pre-IPO securities 'become available to be sold 160 days after the date of the final prospectus' (about 2026-12-07; Investing.com puts it at December 7). Goldman and J.P. Morgan may release early at their discretion; no earnings-triggered early release was found. Only 6.96M shares were sold in the IPO against 64.0M outstanding, and pre-IPO convertible-note holders own ~52%. Uber has a separate staggered lock-up over two years. This overhang may cap any post-print rally, but the unlock itself falls after the window.

Washington DC: after a string of crimes involving rental e-bikes and scooters, micromobility operators including Lime face heightened scrutiny as they seek to renew their permits. The renewal decision is not dated inside the window.

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with. The 20-day run-up of -8.76% and the -49% fall from the high sit beside a modestly positive set of findings; the main negative (Citizens' US trip slowdown) is what the drawdown already reflects, and today's +10% pre-print pop takes back some of the room. So the lean is held to p_up 55.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (a finding inside the guided range is a reported-quarter item the market was told to expect): guide-construction finding cut from +1.0 to +0.6, since consensus already sits in the upper half of the guide.
Rule 5 (a narrow proxy loses to a broader public series): Seattle ride data cut from +0.3 to +0.1, below Citizens' broader public-trip-data read.
Rule 5 (an unexplained move is worth ~0): pre-print +10% positioning finding cut from -0.3 to -0.1.
'A peer's print landing after the company last spoke' (what has worked): European-peer finding left at +0.8.
Rule 6 (keep the finding inside the window): the lock-up (about 2026-12-07) and the DC permit item were already in outside_window, so nothing changed.
abs_move_pct raised from 12 to 13 under the core's note that the hunters' moves run too small (86% realised vol, thin float, first Q4 guide); p_up unchanged at 55.
